A_target.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a [[Definition:Simplex|simplex]] and $g: \Delta \to \Delta$ [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous]].
Then there exists $x \in \Delta$ with $\map g x = x$.

B_source.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Triangulation|triangulation]] of an $n$-simplex with a [[Definition:Sperner Coloring|Sperner coloring]].
Then some cell of $T$ has vertices of all $n + 1$ colors.

substitutions.Sperner coloring: coloring induced by which barycentric coordinate the map g decreases

derived.rainbow sub-simplex: point where g moves no coordinate up, i.e. an approximate fixed point

object_map.reformulation: Color each vertex by a coordinate that g does not increase; a rainbow simplex is then an approximate fixed point, and a limit over finer meshes yields an exact one.

validity_conditions: The coloring rule (color by a non-increasing coordinate) satisfies Sperner's boundary condition, so the lemma applies at every mesh.
The simplex is compact, so the sequence of shrinking rainbow simplices has a convergent subsequence.
g is continuous, so the limit of approximate fixed points is an exact fixed point.
proof_plan:
[[Definition:Triangulation|Triangulate]] $\Delta$ with mesh $\dfrac 1 k$, using barycentric coordinates $x_0, \ldots, x_n$.
Color each vertex $v$ by an index $i$ with $v_i > 0$ and $\map g v_i \le v_i$.

Such $i$ exists, as $\displaystyle \sum_i \map g v_i = \sum_i v_i = 1$.
As $i$ is chosen with $v_i > 0$, a vertex on a face receives a color of that face, so this is a valid [[Definition:Sperner Coloring|Sperner coloring]].
By [[Sperner's Lemma]], there is a rainbow cell $\sigma_k$.

On $\sigma_k$, for each $i$ some vertex $v$ has $\map g v_i \le v_i$.
As the mesh is small, $\sigma_k$ is an approximate fixed point of $g$.

Let $k \to \infty$.
By [[Definition:Compact Space|compactness]], a subsequence of the $\sigma_k$ converges to a point $x$.
By continuity, $\map g x_i \le x_i$ for all $i$; as both sum to $1$, $\map g x = x$.
This proves the [[Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem]].
{{qed}}
